banner: AI 举反例，撼动 87 年数学猜想
banner_en: AI produces a counterexample, shakes an 87-year conjecture

image.caption: AI 首次对开放 87 年的雅可比猜想给出反例：一个从 ℂ³ 到 ℂ³ 的 7 次多项式映射，雅可比行列式恒为非零常数 -2，却将三个不同点映到同一处，因此非全局可逆。三维有反例，更高维自然都有；二维仍未解决，一维早已成立。反例由 Fable AI 找出，菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩（图）7 月 21 日在博客发表《雅可比猜想反例的一次消化》，以尽量少的代数几何阐明其几何结构，并注明自己使用 AI 聊天机器人讨论问题、核对计算。此新闻看点不在数学，而在分工：机器负责生成，专家负责判断与验证。（图：Oberwolfach Photo Collection / Gert-Martin Greuel，CC BY-SA）
image.caption_en: For the first time, AI has produced a counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture, open for 87 years: a degree-7 polynomial map from ℂ³ to ℂ³ whose Jacobian determinant is a nonzero constant (-2) yet which sends three distinct points to the same output, so it is not globally invertible. A counterexample in dimension three means one exists in every higher dimension; the conjecture is still open in two dimensions and was long settled in one. The counterexample was found using Fable AI, and Fields medalist Terence Tao (pictured) wrote up “A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample” on his blog on July 21, explaining its geometric structure with as little algebraic geometry as possible and noting that he used an AI chatbot to discuss the problem and confirm several calculations. The real story here isn't the math, it's the division of labor: the machine generates, the expert judges and verifies. (Image: Oberwolfach Photo Collection / Gert-Martin Greuel, CC BY-SA.)

actions.text: 今晚为你最常用的那个 agent 加一道“信心闸”。今天 HN 上 Cactus 展示了一个易抄的做法：他们没让模型用文字给自己打分（那不靠谱），而是在 Gemma 4 上加了一个仅 6.8 万参数的探针层，读取解码时的隐藏状态，直接预测“本次答错的概率”，AUROC 达 0.814，远高于用熵值作基线的 0.549。有了信心分，便将回答按信心排序，只把最没把握的一小部分（他们测试下来为 15%–35%，视任务而定）送去大模型，其余留在便宜的小模型，整体质量逼近全程使用大模型。你今晚可做：挑一个你反复调优的任务，先用最简陋的信心代理（如答案的 logprob / 自一致性投票的分歧度）为每次调用打分，设一条阈值，只把低于阈值的升级到贵模型，然后量化一件事——到底有多大比例真的需要升级。多半比你想象得少得多。Cactus 的探针代码在 Transformers / MLX / Llama.cpp 中均已开源，若想做得正经，直接上它。
actions.source: Hacker News · Show HN：Cactus Hybrid — 教会 Gemma 4 知道自己什么时候错了
actions.text_en: Add a “confidence gate” to your most-used agent tonight. On HN today, Cactus showed a very copyable approach: instead of having the model rate itself in text (unreliable), they bolted a tiny 68k-parameter probe onto Gemma 4 that reads the hidden states during decoding and directly predicts the probability the answer is wrong — 0.814 AUROC, far above the 0.549 you get from an entropy baseline. With that confidence score, sort answers by confidence and send only the least-confident slice (they measured 15–35%, depending on task) up to a big cloud model, keeping the rest on a cheap small model, and overall quality approaches running the big model everywhere. What you can do tonight: pick a task you keep tuning, score each call with the crudest confidence proxy you have (the answer's logprob, or the disagreement rate of a self-consistency vote), set a threshold, escalate only the calls below it to the expensive model, and then measure one thing — what fraction actually needed to go up. It's usually far less than you'd guess. Cactus open-sourced the probe for Transformers / MLX / Llama.cpp, so use it directly if you want to do it properly.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Show HN: Cactus Hybrid — we taught Gemma 4 to know when it's wrong

actions.text: 今晚花二十分钟，把所有会被客户看到的 AI 生成物过一遍，凡是“一看就是 AI”的，列出来准备手工重做。今天 HN 上一篇讲餐馆用 AI 重做菜单的文章点破一件反直觉的事：设计的精致程度与背后投入的心力，如今已零相关；于是那种“闻着像 AI”的直接产出，正从省事变成负资产。高赞评论一刀见血——一件小事你都糊弄，客户自会默认你别处也糊弄；AI 生成的菜品图还常常货不对板，恐怖谷般地让人不想点。对做 GTM / 品牌的人，这不是审美洁癖，而是信任信号在打折。做法：将落地页首图、产品截图、菜单或目录图、社媒配图、邮件模板中的 AI 生成图列出，凡是假模假样、恐怖谷的，标记重做，宁可用真实照片或朴素排版，也别用一眼假的 AI 图。记一条原则：AI 图能省时间，但省下的时间不该花在客户的第一印象上。
actions.source: Hacker News · 那些把菜单用 AI 重做丑了的商家
actions.text_en: Spend twenty minutes tonight going through every AI-generated asset a customer will see, and list the ones that obviously read as AI to redo by hand. A piece on HN today about restaurants using AI to redesign their menus lands a counterintuitive point: the polish of a design now has zero relation to the effort behind it, so output that “smells like AI” is turning from a shortcut into a liability. A top comment nails it — if you're careless about one small thing, customers assume you're careless about the rest; and AI-generated food photos often misrepresent the actual dish, uncannily unappetizing enough to put people off ordering. For anyone doing GTM/brand, this isn't aesthetic fussiness, it's a discount on your trust signal. How: list the AI-generated images in your landing-page hero, product screenshots, menu/catalog art, social graphics, and email templates; flag the fake, uncanny ones to redo, and prefer a real photo or plain typography over an image that's visibly AI. Keep one principle: AI images save time, but the time saved shouldn't come out of your customer's first impression.
actions.source_en: Hacker News · Businesses with ugly AI menu redesigns

actions.text: 给你正在盯的那个北极星指标做一次“有无被刷”的体检，照 Dylan Castillo 测 pelicanmaxxing 的法子来。有人怀疑各家大模型在偷偷针对 Simon 那个“鹈鹕骑自行车”的 SVG 梗做优化，他没停在猜：跑了 8 种动物 × 6 种载具共 1008 张 SVG，用一个模型当裁判逐张打分，再用固定效应回归把“这道题本身难不难”扣掉，结论是几乎没有针对性刷分的证据（鹈鹕在 8 种动物中质量只排第 6，恰恰相反）。可迁移的是这套动作，而非这个结论：当你担心某个指标被人、或被你自己模型刷时，别靠感觉，造一批对照样本、找个中立裁判逐条判、再把难度差异回归掉。做法：挑一个你最依赖的指标，写下它最可能被钻的三个空子，各造 20–50 个样本跑一遍，看分数是否被异常抬高。如果你无法判断自己的核心指标有无被刷，你其实是在盲飞。
actions.source: 文摘 · Dylan Castillo：各家大模型在给鹈鹕刷分吗？
actions.text_en: Run a “is this being gamed?” checkup on the north-star metric you're watching, the way Dylan Castillo tested for pelicanmaxxing. Some suspected the labs were quietly optimizing for Simon Willison's “pelican riding a bicycle” SVG meme, and instead of guessing he ran the numbers: 1,008 SVGs across 8 animals × 6 vehicles, scored one by one by a judge model, then a fixed-effects regression to subtract out how hard each prompt inherently is — concluding there's little evidence of targeted gaming (pelicans ranked only 6th of 8 animals on quality, the opposite of what gaming would predict). What transfers is the procedure, not the verdict: when you worry a metric is being gamed — by someone, or by your own model — don't go on feel; build a batch of controlled samples, have a neutral judge score each, and regress out the difficulty differences. How: pick a metric you lean on hardest, write down the three most likely ways it could be gamed, generate 20–50 samples for each, and run them to see if the score gets abnormally inflated. If you can't tell whether your core metric is being gamed, you're flying blind.
actions.source_en: Digest · Dylan Castillo: Are AI labs pelicanmaxxing?

hands_on.title: 今晚 30 分钟：把一个脚本的模型调用换成 Ramp Router，看它替你选模型
hands_on.why: 今天满版都在绕同一件事：“能过质量线的最便宜模型”是个每周都在动的移动靶。Ramp 把自家内部用了三年、每月路由 2.75 万亿 token、替自己砍了 30% AI 成本的路由器开放了：一个 OpenAI 兼容端点，自动为每个请求挑“能过质量线的最便宜模型”，每周拿真实流量重测新模型并自动改路由，还带缓存和供应商故障切换。对做 GTM / 成本的人，这是把“该用哪个模型”从一个你每周手工纠结的决定，变成一条基础设施。三十分钟你就能亲手感受：同一批调用交给路由器后落到了哪些模型、省了多少，而不是停在概念上。
steps: 打开 https://ramp.com/router/ ，按页面加入 waitlist 拿 API key（前 500 名有 100 美元额度；发布期按 token 列表价计费，不额外收路由费）
找一个你现成的、用 OpenAI SDK 的脚本，把 base_url 改成 Ramp Router 给的端点、key 换成它的（官方称改一行即可）
用你平时那批请求原样跑一遍，别动 prompt，让它自己为每个请求挑模型
打开它的用量 / 路由面板，看每个请求实际落到了哪个模型、单次成本多少，和你原来固定用一个模型相比省了多少
记一条判断：哪些请求它敢降级到便宜模型、哪些留在贵的。这条“最便宜够用”的线每周都在移动，正是今天满版在讲的事（详见今日自我升级）
hands_on.source: 文摘 · TLDR AI：Ramp Router（Ramp 的 LLM 网关）
hands_on.title_en: Tonight, 30 minutes: swap one script's model calls to Ramp Router and watch it pick the model for you
hands_on.why_en: The whole issue today circles one thing: the “cheapest model that clears the quality bar” is a target that moves every week. Ramp has opened up its internal router — three years old, routing 2.75 trillion tokens a month, and credited with cutting Ramp's own AI costs 30%: one OpenAI-compatible endpoint that automatically picks the cheapest model that clears a quality bar for each request, re-tests new models on real traffic every week and reroutes automatically, and layers caching and provider fallback on top. For anyone doing GTM/cost, this turns “which model should I use” from a decision you re-litigate by hand each week into a piece of infrastructure. In thirty minutes you can feel it directly: for the same batch of calls, which models the router lands on and how much it saves — instead of leaving it as a concept.
steps_en: Open https://ramp.com/router/ , join the waitlist to get an API key (first 500 get $100 in credits; at launch you pay list price per token with no extra routing fee)
Take an existing script that uses the OpenAI SDK, change base_url to the Ramp Router endpoint and swap in its key (they say it's a one-line change)
Run your usual batch of requests as-is, don't touch the prompts, and let it pick a model per request
Open its usage/routing dashboard and see which model each request actually landed on, the per-call cost, and how much you saved versus pinning one model

Note one judgment: which requests it dares downgrade to a cheap model and which it keeps on the expensive one. That “cheapest that's good enough” line moves every week — which is exactly what the whole issue is about (see today's self-upgrade)
hands_on.source_en: Digest · TLDR AI: Ramp Router (Ramp's LLM gateway)

meta_read: 把今天几条并排看，落点不在模型又强了多少，而在一件更不显眼的事：能把模型产出用好的那层判断力，正在变成稀缺品。AI 头一次对开放 87 年的雅可比猜想举出反例，但这条新闻能站得住，靠的是陶哲轩能把它复核、消化、讲清楚，还老实标注哪几步是让 AI 帮着核对的。同一天，餐馆老板按下“AI 重做菜单”的按钮，出来的是没人想点的恐怖谷菜品。同一个工具，两种相反的结果，差别就在有没有那层人的判断。再看另外两条：Ramp 把内部路由器开放，它每天替 2.75 万亿 token 挑“能过质量线的最便宜模型”，值钱的不是哪个模型，而是“够用就好”这条线画在哪，而且每周重画一次；Dylan Castillo 怀疑各家在偷偷给鹈鹕梗刷分，没停在猜，跑了 1008 张图、找裁判、扣掉难度做回归，才敢说证据不足。四件事其实是一回事：AI 把“生产”变得极其便宜，于是稀缺的输入换成了判断力——判断哪个产出可信（Tao 复核，Cactus 干脆教模型给自己的答案打信心分）、哪个模型够用（Ramp）、哪个指标是真的（Castillo），以及什么东西压根不该发出去（那份 AI 菜单）。这把前两天那条线再往前推一格：前天说值钱的挪到了模型外面那层安排，昨天问那层安排替谁干活，今天说那层安排里最硬的一块，是人的辨别力和品味。这与“AI 取代专家”的流行说法正好反着：它反而抬高了专业和眼力的回报。Tao 的反例能被“消化”，因为一位菲尔兹奖得主判得动它；那份菜单沦为 slop，因为老板判不动。对独立建设者，今天能落地的也在这层。一，别再手工纠结该用哪个模型，把“最便宜够用”做成一条会自己更新的规则（详见今日上手与自我升级）。二，给你的 agent 加一道信心闸，让它知道自己什么时候没把握，只把没把握的送上去（详见一版行动）。三，凡是客户会看到的 AI 生成物，先问一句它是不是“一看就是 AI”，是就手工重做，如今这股味道是负资产，不是省事（详见二版行动）。今天没有一条在说人要靠边站，说的都是：机器负责生成，你得负责判断。
meta_read_en: Line up today's items and the point isn't how much stronger the models got — it's a quieter thing: the layer of judgment that puts model output to good use is becoming the scarce input. AI produced a counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture, open for 87 years, but the news holds up only because Terence Tao could verify, digest, and explain it — and honestly noted which steps he had the AI help confirm. The same day, a restaurant owner pressed the “redesign my menu with AI” button and got uncanny, no-one-wants-to-order-this dishes. Same tool, opposite outcomes, and the difference is whether there's a human judgment layer. Two more: Ramp opened its internal router, which picks the cheapest model that clears a quality bar for 2.75 trillion tokens a day — the value isn't any one model, it's where you draw the “good enough” line, redrawn weekly; and Dylan Castillo, suspecting the labs were quietly gaming the pelican meme, didn't stop at suspicion but ran 1,008 images, a judge, and a difficulty-adjusted regression before saying the evidence isn't there. All four are the same thing: AI makes production dirt cheap, so the scarce input becomes discernment — judging which output to trust (Tao verifying; Cactus outright teaching a model to score its own confidence), which model is enough (Ramp), which metric is real (Castillo), and what shouldn't ship at all (that AI menu). This advances the last two days by one notch: two days ago the value moved out to the arrangement around the model; yesterday, whom that arrangement works for; today, the hardest part of that arrangement is human discernment and taste. It runs opposite to the fashionable “AI replaces the expert” line — it actually raises the return on expertise and an eye for quality. Tao's counterexample could be “digested” because a Fields medalist could evaluate it; the menu became slop because the owner couldn't. For solo builders, the actionable part is in that layer too. (1) Stop re-litigating which model to use by hand — make “cheapest that's good enough” a rule that updates itself (see hands-on and self-upgrade). (2) Add a confidence gate to your agent so it knows when it's unsure and sends only the unsure calls up (see Action 1). (3) For any AI-generated asset a customer will see, first ask whether it obviously reads as AI, and if so redo it by hand — that smell is now a liability, not a shortcut (see Action 2). Nothing today says humans step aside; it all says: the machine generates, you have to judge.

learned: 读台账，最近七条全长在同一根轴上：用评测把一个多 agent 循环管好、管省（二元评测→按努力档升级→弃权门→多供应商 fail over→成本诊断→按角色分档→能力隔离的评测门）。它们都在决定：一个子任务失败后加多大力、用哪个档、怎么保证打分门本身不被糊弄。但它们默认路由表是静的：哪个模型算“最便宜够用”一旦定了就不动。今天 Ramp 把自家内部用了三年的路由器开放，正好戳中这个盲点——它每周拿真实流量重测新模型、自动改路由，因为在 Kimi / GLM / Gemini Flash 一周一个新开源旗舰的市场里，“最便宜够用”那条线本身每周都在移动。

所以补一条：别把“某类子任务该用哪个模型”当成开工时定一次的静态决定，把它做成一条在滚动窗口上不断重估的策略——用真实的、被评过的产出当反馈，像多臂老虎机（Thompson sampling）那样，让一个刚变得够便宜的模型自动被提上来，一个悄悄退步的自动被降下去，不用我每周手动重排。它接在 07-21“按角色分档”之后（那条把强弱模型各就各位），把那套分档从静态变成活的；也和 07-20“成本诊断”不同（那条是失败后的一次性体检，这条是持续、自动的重估）。灵感来自今天开放的 Ramp Router（每月 2.75 万亿 token，替自己砍了 30% 成本，每周重测加自动改路由加供应商故障切换）。
new_capabilities: 🎯（云端提议，待笔记本采纳）“滚动窗口在线路由（bandit 刷新的模型档位）”（rolling-window online routing）：在整条升级阶梯的地基上再加一层。以前我把“哪类活用哪个模型”当成开工时定一次的静态分档；现在把它做成一条会自己更新的策略——在一个滚动窗口上，用真实的、被评过的产出当反馈，用 bandit / Thompson sampling 持续重估每类子任务的“最便宜够用”模型，一个新近变够便宜的自动升档，一个退步的自动降档，不用我手动重排。它建立在 07-21“按角色分档”之上（把分档从静态变活的），与 07-20“成本诊断”互补（那条一次性、事后，这条持续、自动）。灵感来自今天开放的 Ramp Router。已作为 proposed（cloud）追加进 ota-ledger.md，交 Zen 笔记本 Claude 下次落地。调用意图：“把模型路由做成滚动窗口上的 bandit，用真实评测结果做反馈，自动升/降档，别把‘最便宜够用’写死。”
learned_en: Reading the ledger, the last seven lines all sit on one axis: using evals to run a multi-agent loop well and cheaply (binary evals → effort-tier escalation → the abstain gate → provider-diverse fail over → cost-per-outcome check → planner/worker cost-tiering by role → capability-scoped eval gates). They all decide how much force to add after a subtask fails, which tier to use, and how to keep the scoring gate itself from being gamed. But they silently assume the routing table is static: once “which model is the cheapest that's good enough” is set, it stays put. Today Ramp opened up its three-year-old internal router, which stabs exactly that blind spot — it re-tests new models on real traffic every week and reroutes automatically, because in a market shipping a new open-weight flagship (Kimi/GLM/Gemini Flash) every week, the “cheapest that's good enough” line itself moves weekly.

So I'm adding a line: stop treating “which model for this class of subtask” as a static, decided-once-at-the-start choice, and make it a policy that's continuously re-estimated over a rolling window — with real, graded output as feedback, bandit / Thompson-sampling style, so a model that just became cheap enough is auto-promoted and one that quietly regressed is auto-demoted, without me re-shuffling by hand each week. It follows 07-21's cost-tiering by role (which puts the strong and weak models in their places) by making those tier assignments live instead of static; and it differs from 07-20's cost-per-outcome check (a one-shot post-failure diagnostic — this is continuous and automatic). Inspired by today's Ramp Router (2.75T tokens/month, cut its own costs 30%, weekly re-test plus auto-reroute plus provider fallback).
new_capabilities_en: 🎯 (cloud-proposed, pending laptop adoption) “Rolling-window online routing (bandit-refreshed model tiers)”: another layer on the foundation of the whole escalation ladder. Previously I treated “which model for which work” as a static tiering decided once at the start; now I make it a self-updating policy — over a rolling window, using real graded output as feedback, a bandit / Thompson-sampling loop continuously re-estimates the cheapest-good-enough model for each class of subtask, auto-promoting one that just became cheap enough and auto-demoting one that regressed, with no manual re-shuffle. It builds on 07-21's cost-tiering by role (making the tiers live instead of static) and complements 07-20's cost-per-outcome check (that one is one-shot and after the fact; this is continuous and automatic). Inspired by today's newly-opened Ramp Router. Appended as proposed (cloud) to ota-ledger.md for Zen's laptop Claude to land next session. Invoke intent: “keep model routing as a rolling-window bandit over real graded outcomes; auto-promote a newly-cheap-enough model and auto-demote a regressed one — don't hardcode the ‘cheapest good enough.’”

items.title: 陶哲轩的 ChatGPT 对话：消化雅可比猜想的那个反例
items.title_en: Terence Tao's ChatGPT conversation about the Jacobian Conjecture counterexample
items.author: Terence Tao · Hacker News
items.flag: ⚠️ 反例目前只在三维及以上成立，二维仍未解决，一维早已成立，不是“整个雅可比猜想被推翻”。反例由 Fable AI 找出，据报道是 Anthropic 的 Fable 模型；由菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩复核、消化并公开注明用 AI 核对过若干计算，属可信的专家背书，但完整同行评议仍在进行，技术细节以正式论文为准。
items.flag_en: ⚠️ The counterexample holds only in dimension three and above; two dimensions remains open and one dimension was long settled — this is not “the whole Jacobian Conjecture overturned.” It was found using Fable AI, reportedly an Anthropic Fable model, and was verified and digested by Fields medalist Terence Tao, who openly noted he used AI to confirm several calculations — credible expert endorsement, but full peer review is ongoing, so treat the technical details as provisional pending the formal paper.
items.summary: AI 首次为一项提出 87 年的著名猜想举出反例。雅可比猜想断言：若从 ℂⁿ 到 ℂⁿ 的多项式映射的雅可比行列式为非零常数，则该映射可逆，且逆也是多项式。如今在 ℂ³ 上发现了反例：一个 7 次多项式映射，雅可比行列式恒为 -2，却将三个不同点——(0,0,-1/4)、(1,-3/2,13/2)、(-1,3/2,13/2)——映射到同一点。因此映射局部可逆，但全局不可逆。三维有反例，更高维亦然；二维仍未解决，一维早已证毕。反例由 Fable AI 发现，随后 GPT-5.6 Sol/Codex 在此基础上生成一篇“论文”，给出整族更高维反例。菲尔兹奖得主陶哲轩 7 月 21 日在博客发表《雅可比猜想反例的一次消化》，作为个人消化练习，用最少代数几何阐明反例的几何结构（核心直觉：线性式与二次式相乘得三次式，同一三次式有不同分解方式，故不同点映射至同一像），并明确写道：“我用了一个 AI 聊天机器人来讨论该问题的各方面并核对若干计算。”陶哲轩并非声称自己发现，而是担任复核、消化与提供直觉的角色；同日他还公开了与 ChatGPT 逐步理解反例的对话记录。HN 上从业者观点一致：要用 AI 攻克硬核问题，前提是有能力判断其回答对错（“我能用 AI 写代码，因我写了数十年代码；我不能用它做理论物理，因我无法判断其回答”）。有效用法是短促精准的追问，用行话将其拉至你的水平，大力纠偏，并预期它会一脸笃定地给出错误答案，最好再用另一模型交叉验证。
items.summary_en: For the first time, AI has produced a counterexample to a famous, 87-year-open conjecture. The Jacobian Conjecture says a polynomial map from ℂⁿ to ℂⁿ with a nonzero constant Jacobian determinant must be invertible with a polynomial inverse. There is now a counterexample in ℂ³: a degree-7 polynomial map with Jacobian determinant a constant -2 that nonetheless sends three distinct points ((0,0,-1/4), (1,-3/2,13/2), (-1,3/2,13/2)) to the same output, so it's locally but not globally invertible. A counterexample in dimension three means one exists in all higher dimensions; two dimensions remains open and one was long settled. The counterexample was found using Fable AI, after which GPT-5.6 Sol/Codex wrote up a “paper” giving a whole family of higher-dimensional counterexamples. Fields medalist Terence Tao published “A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample” on July 21 as a digestion exercise for himself, explaining the geometric structure with as little algebraic geometry as possible (the core intuition: multiplying a linear form by a quadratic gives a cubic, and one cubic can factor multiple ways, so different points map to the same place), and stated plainly, “I used an AI chatbot to discuss various aspects of this problem and to confirm several of the calculations made here.” He doesn't claim to have discovered it; his role is to verify, digest, and give intuition — and the same day he posted his ChatGPT session working through the counterexample step by step. Practitioners on HN converge on one read: being able to use AI on hard problems presupposes you can judge whether its answers are right (“I can use AI for coding after decades of coding; I can't use it for theoretical physics because I can't evaluate the responses”); the effective mode is short pointed questions, using the field's jargon to pull it to your level, steering it hard, and expecting it to state wrong things in a confident professorial tone — ideally cross-checking with a second model.
items.why: 本期头条，亦为社评支点。这并非又一次跑分，而是一个分水岭：AI 首次为开放 87 年的著名猜想举出反例。而此事真正站得住，靠的是菲尔兹奖得主将其复核、消化、讲清。对 AI 应用开发者而言，可迁移的并非数学本身，而是这套分工——AI 负责生成，专家负责判断与验证。陶哲轩的价值不在计算，而在判断哪一步可信、如何结构化，以及坦诚说明哪些步骤由 AI 核对。这条线正是社评要展开的：当生成变得廉价，稀缺的输入就转变为判断力。注意：反例仅对三维及以上成立，二维仍悬而未决，完整同行评议尚在进行。
items.why_en: The issue's lead and the pivot of the editorial. Not another benchmark — a concrete watershed: for the first time AI produced a counterexample to a famous 87-year-open conjecture. What makes it hold up is that a Fields medalist could verify, digest, and explain it. For anyone building AI products, what transfers isn't the math but the division of labor — the machine generates, the expert judges and verifies. Tao's value isn't computing; it's judging which steps to trust, structuring the result, and being honest about which parts he had AI confirm. That's the line the editorial develops: when generation gets cheap, the scarce input becomes discernment. Read it with the flag: it holds only in dimension three and above, two dimensions is still open, and peer review is ongoing.

items.title: Show HN：Cactus Hybrid —— 我们教会了 Gemma 4 知道自己什么时候错了
items.title_en: Show HN: Cactus Hybrid — we taught Gemma 4 to know when it's wrong
items.author: Cactus · Hacker News
items.summary: Cactus 将 Gemma 4 post-train 成一个可对自身答案标注信心分数（0-1）的本地模型：开发者据此将低信心请求转至云端大模型，高信心请求留本地，仅将 15%-35% 的请求上云，即可逼近全程使用云端大模型的质量。其方法并非让模型用文字自评（不可靠），也非简单看 token 熵，而是附加一个仅 6.8 万参数的探针层，读取解码时的隐藏状态，直接预测“本次答错的概率”。探针采用 LayerNorm、低秩投影、注意力池化及小型 MLP 头，所提取的正确性信号与模态无关——在完全未见音频训练数据的情况下，对音频任务的 AUROC 仍达 0.79-0.88。整体在 12 个基准上探针 AUROC 为 0.814，而熵值基线仅为 0.549；不同任务的上云比例不同（ChartQA 约 15%-20%，MMLU-Pro 约 45%-55%）。评论区有人指出：模型严格来说只能测到“不确定/不自洽”，不等于真正知道自己的“错误”；团队也承认当前局限：仅支持单序列解码、按任务整体路由比逐 token 更靠谱、且每个模型需单独训练探针。代码已对 Transformers、MLX、Llama.cpp 开源，Ollama/vLLM 支持正在路上。
items.summary_en: Cactus post-trained Gemma 4 into an on-device model that attaches a confidence score (0–1) to its answers: developers route low-confidence requests to a big cloud model and keep high-confidence ones local, sending only 15–35% of requests up while approaching cloud-model quality. The method isn't text self-rating (unreliable) or plain token entropy, but a tiny 68k-parameter probe that reads the hidden states during decoding and directly predicts the probability the answer is wrong; the probe uses LayerNorm, a low-rank projection, attention pooling, and a small MLP head, and the correctness signal it extracts is modality-independent — with zero audio training data it still hits 0.79–0.88 AUROC on audio tasks. Overall the probe reaches 0.814 AUROC across 12 benchmarks versus 0.549 for an entropy baseline; the route-up fraction varies by task (ChartQA ~15–20%, MMLU-Pro ~45–55%). A commenter pushes back that a model can strictly only detect “uncertainty/inconsistency,” not true wrongness; the team acknowledges current limits: single-sequence decoding only, per-task routing works better than per-step, and each model needs its own probe trained. Code is open-sourced for Transformers, MLX, and Llama.cpp, with Ollama/vLLM support coming.
items.why: 本期 builder 主力之一，直接提供可操作方案。它将“让模型自知何时没有把握”从口号变为可复用的机制：一个数万参数的探针，读取隐藏状态预测错误概率，据此仅将少数没把握的请求升级。对独立开发者而言，此法既省钱（多数请求留在便宜或本地模型），又更稳健（该升级时才升级），将本报反复提及的“信心/弃权”概念落地为具体产品形态。评论中“它测的是不确定，而非真实错误”这一提醒值得谨记，切勿将信心分等同于正确性保证。
items.why_en: One of the issue's builder anchors, feeding Action 1 directly. It turns “let the model know when it's unsure” from a slogan into a copyable mechanism: a tens-of-thousands-parameter probe that reads hidden states to predict the error probability, then escalates only the unsure minority of requests. For solo builders it's both cheaper (most requests stay on a cheap/local model) and safer (only what should escalate does) — a concrete picture of building the “confidence/abstention” idea this paper keeps raising into a product. Keep the comment that “it detects uncertainty, not true wrongness” in mind — don't treat a confidence score as a correctness guarantee.

items.title: 那些把菜单用 AI 重做丑了的商家
items.title_en: Businesses with ugly AI menu redesigns
items.author: Fiddery Blog · Hacker News
items.summary: 一篇短文加 HN 热议，讲述一个正在蔓延的现象：不懂设计的小商家用生成式 AI 一键重做菜单和门面物料，“看到按钮就按”，结果满屏恐怖谷般的假菜品图片，让人毫无食欲。作者以一家菲律宾/夏威夷餐馆为例：AI 重做的 spamsilog 拼盘与真实食物摆在一起，生成图假得离谱，而真菜其实地道。评论点破更深层问题：如今设计的精致程度与背后投入的心力已无关联，因此抛光本身不再构成信号——一件小事都糊弄，客户会默认你其他地方也糊弄。AI 直接产出以及“闻着像 AI”的东西，正因为商品化而越来越不受待见（“低努力的产品会被低努力的公司使用；一家‘高端’店配上 AI 菜单加 AI 装修，是个坏信号”）。还有人担心整条街被 AI 图同质化，抹掉本地辨识度。结论：真正想在品味上被记住的经营者，会继续花人力做出人类做得出的东西。
items.summary_en: A short post plus a lively HN thread on a spreading phenomenon: small businesses with no design skill use generative AI to one-click redesign menus and storefront materials — “see button, they press” — and end up with screens of uncanny, unappetizing food images no one wants to order. The author cites a Filipino/Hawaiian restaurant: the AI-redone spamsilog platter next to the real one looks grotesquely fake, while the actual food is authentic. The comments surface the deeper point: the polish of a design now has zero relation to the effort behind it, so polish itself has stopped being a signal — be careless about one small thing and customers assume you're careless about the rest; direct AI output, and anything that “smells like AI,” is increasingly disliked precisely because it's commodified (“low-effort products get used by low-effort companies; a ‘high-end’ place with an AI menu and AI decor is a bad sign”); others worry a whole street gets homogenized by AI imagery, erasing local identity. The takeaway: businesses that actually want to be remembered for taste keep paying humans to make recognizably human output.
items.why: 选它，是为了给满版“AI 让一切更便宜”钉一个反面注脚，同时直接为二版提供素材。讲的是同一枚硬币的背面：生成成本趋近于零时，缺乏判断力的一方会直接翻车——省下的时间恰恰砸在了客户的第一印象上。对做 GTM 和品牌的人，可迁移的判断是：“闻着像 AI”如今是负资产，不是省事；抛光不等于用心，客户会据此反推你的整体可靠度。它与头条形成对照：Tao 有判断力，把 AI 产出消化成了成果；那些老板没有，把 AI 产出变成了 slop。
items.why_en: Picked as a counterweight to the issue's “AI makes everything cheaper,” and it feeds Action 2 directly. It's the flip side of the same coin: when generation goes to zero cost, the end that lacks judgment simply crashes — the time saved lands squarely on the customer's first impression. For anyone doing GTM/brand, the transferable judgment is that “smells like AI” is now a liability, not a shortcut; polish no longer equals care, and customers reason backward from it to your overall reliability. It mirrors the lead: Tao had the judgment to digest AI output into a result; these owners didn't, and turned AI output into slop.

items.title: Ramp Router：把内部用了三年的 LLM 网关开放出来
items.title_en: Ramp Router: opening up a three-year-old internal LLM gateway
items.author: TLDR AI
items.summary: Ramp 将自家用了三年的 LLM 路由器开放给所有人。它本是内部工具，用来把 100 多个 AI 功能各自绑定到合适的模型，如今每月路由 2.75 万亿 token，帮 Ramp 把 AI 成本削减了约 30%。对外就是一个 OpenAI 兼容端点：将每个请求发给“能过质量线的最便宜模型”，每周用真实流量重测新模型并自动调整路由，加之缓存和压缩，某供应商宕机或限流时自动切换到别家。接入几乎零成本——只需改一行 base_url。发布期免费（按 token 列表价计费，不额外收路由费），waitlist 前 500 名送 100 美元额度。Ramp 的工程博客还披露了其使用 Thompson sampling 等在线学习算法做路由决策，即路由策略是持续跟随真实反馈更新的，而非一张写死的表。
items.summary_en: Ramp opened its three-year-old internal LLM router to everyone. It began as internal tooling to keep 100+ AI features each pinned to the right model, and today routes 2.75 trillion tokens a month, having cut Ramp's AI costs by about 30%. To the outside it's a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint: it sends each request to the cheapest model that clears a quality bar, re-tests new models on real traffic every week and reroutes automatically, layers caching and compression, and fails over to another provider when one goes down or rate-limits. Adoption is near-zero-cost — OpenAI-compatible, a one-line base_url change. It's free at launch (list price per token, no extra routing fee), and the first 500 off the waitlist get $100 in credits. Ramp's engineering blog notes the routing decisions run on online learning like Thompson sampling, i.e. the routing policy keeps updating from real feedback rather than being a hardcoded table.
items.why: 本期 GTM/成本主力，直接为“今日上手”提供素材，也是今日自我升级的灵感来源。它把“该用哪个模型”从每周手工纠结变成一项基础设施，最关键的一点常被忽略：它每周用真实流量重测、自动改路由——因为开源旗舰一周一换，最便宜够用的线每周都在移动。对做增长和成本的人，这是今晚能接上、明天能看账单的东西（改一行、免费起步）。它也与头条呼应：值钱的不是哪个模型，而是把“够用就好”的线画在哪里，并让它自动更新。
items.why_en: The issue's GTM/cost anchor, feeding the hands-on and the inspiration for today's self-upgrade. It turns “which model to use” from a weekly hand-wringing exercise into infrastructure, and the most important part is easy to miss: it re-tests on real traffic weekly and reroutes automatically — because in a market that swaps open-weight flagships every week, the “cheapest good enough” line itself moves weekly. For anyone doing growth/cost, it's something you can wire up tonight and read on tomorrow's bill (one-line change, free to start). It also rhymes with the lead: the value isn't any one model, it's where you draw the “good enough” line and whether it updates itself.

items.title: 各家大模型在给鹈鹕刷分吗？
items.author: Dylan Castillo
items.summary: Simon Willison 那个“让模型画一只骑自行车的鹈鹕 SVG”的梗火成了非正式基准，于是有人怀疑各家在偷偷针对它优化（benchmaxxing 的鹈鹕版，pelicanmaxxing）。Dylan Castillo 没有止于猜测，动手测试：取 7 个前沿模型（GPT-5.6 Terra、Claude Sonnet 5、Gemini 3.5 Flash、Grok 4.5、Qwen3.7-Max、GLM-5.2、DeepSeek V4 Pro），排出 8 种动物×6 种载具的 48 个 prompt，总共生成 1008 张 SVG，用 GPT-5.6 Luna 当裁判逐张给“动物像不像、载具像不像、动作合不合理”打 1-5 分，再用固定效应回归剔除各组合本身的难度。结论是几乎找不到针对鹈鹕刷分的证据：鹈鹕在 8 种动物里质量排第 6，自行车在 6 种载具里排第 7，与“被专门优化”正好相反；回归后没有哪个模型在鹈鹕、自行车或两者组合上显著变好（只有 Gemini 的自行车项勉强达 p=0.022，多重比较校正后消失，属预期内的假阳性）。他也留了余地：单独针对这个组合刷分没看到，但更宽泛的“SVGmaxxing/图像整体优化”仍可能存在，且更难查。
items.summary_en: Simon Willison's “draw a pelican riding a bicycle as SVG” bit got popular enough to become an informal benchmark, so some suspected labs were quietly optimizing for it (the pelican version of benchmaxxing — pelicanmaxxing). Dylan Castillo didn't stop at suspicion and tested it: he took 7 frontier models (GPT-5.6 Terra, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.5 Flash, Grok 4.5, Qwen3.7-Max, GLM-5.2, DeepSeek V4 Pro), laid out a 48-prompt grid of 8 animals × 6 vehicles, generated 1,008 SVGs, scored each 1–5 on animal/vehicle/action coherence with GPT-5.6 Luna as judge, then ran a fixed-effects regression to subtract out each combo's inherent difficulty. The conclusion: little evidence of pelican-specific gaming — pelicans ranked only 6th of 8 animals and bicycles 7th of 6 vehicles on quality, the opposite of “targeted optimization”; after regression no lab was significantly better on pelicans, bicycles, or the combo (only Gemini's bicycle effect barely hit p=0.022, which vanishes under multiple-comparison correction — an expected false positive). He leaves room, though: no gaming of this specific combo, but broader “SVGmaxxing / general image optimization” could still exist and is harder to detect.
items.why: 选它不为结论，为方法，直接为三版行动提供素材。它给出了“怎么判断一个指标是否被刷”的可操作方案：造对照样本、找中立裁判逐条评判、再用回归剔除难度差异，让结论不靠感觉说话。对盯 S&O 和增长指标的人，这套方法可以照搬到自己的北极星指标上。它也与本报评测线一致：一个无法验证是否被刷的指标，和一个无法承认自己不确定的裁判一样危险。放在 Tao 那条旁边看更清楚——同样是面对 AI，一个动手验证，一个止于猜测，差别就是判断力那一层。
items.why_en: Picked not for the verdict but the method, feeding Action 3 directly. It offers a copyable procedure for judging whether a metric is being gamed: build controlled samples, have a neutral judge score each, then regress out difficulty differences so you're not arguing from feel. For anyone watching S&O/growth metrics, this checkup ports straight onto your own north star. It's of a piece with this paper's eval thread: a metric you can't verify isn't being gamed is as dangerous as a judge that can't admit it's unsure. Next to Tao it reads clearer — same confrontation with AI, one verifies, one stops at guessing, and the difference is that layer of judgment.

notes: 云端无头运行（GitHub Actions，America/New_York）：本期由两条无头渠道独立凑齐——Hacker News（扫描头版约 60 条，选取 AI/LLM/agent/开发工具/独立建设相关高分帖，逐条进入评论与原文/权威来源交叉核实）与“文摘”（TLDR AI 的 RSS+Ramp 官方页；Dylan Castillo 博客长文）。两平台达标（≥2 来源、5 条），故 partial=false，无缺席横幅。头条雅可比反例以陶哲轩本人博客《A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample》（terrytao.wordpress.com，07-21）为权威源核对：反例仅在三维及以上成立，二维仍开放；发现用的是 Fable AI，由 Tao 复核消化并注明用 AI 核对过计算，故按“可信但未走完同行评议”加 flag，不夸大为“整个猜想被推翻”。刻意避开昨日已覆盖的条目（ChatGPT 广告、OpenAI/Hugging Face 越权事件、Gemini Flash Cyber、Anthropic 和解、Claude Code 炉边对话、Nativ）；也主动将主题从昨日的安全/激励对齐挪开，换到“生成变便宜、判断力变稀缺”这条不同线上，保证跨期多样性。
